arguments.value: Donald L. Graham is a senior United States district judge for the Southern District of Florida, taking senior status in 2013 after more than two decades on the bench. Born in Salisbury, North Carolina, in 1948, he earned his B.A. from West Virginia State College in 1971 and his J.D. from the Ohio State University College of Law in 1974. He began his legal career as a U.S. Army major in the Judge Advocate General’s Corps and later served as an assistant U.S. attorney in the Southern District of Florida, while also maintaining private practice in Miami and serving as an adjunct instructor at the University of Maryland. Nominated to the federal bench by President George H. W. Bush in 1991, he was confirmed by the Senate and received his commission later that year.
